arktisch.et: Learned borrowing from Latin arcticus, from Ancient Greek ἀρκτικός (arktikós).

s: Arcadia (district or prefecture in the Peloponnese)

Arklitten.et: From the earlier form Arkeliten (attested in 1359), Erkeliten (1401), from Old Prussian. (Folk etymology connects the name to the fact that the place had arg gelitten (“suffered terribly”) during the Swedish chapter of the Thirty Years' War.)

Arkade.et: From French arcade (early 17th cent.), from Italian arcata
